# Third Normal Form

A relation is in 3NF when every non-key attribute depends on the key, the whole key, and nothing but
the key. In practice: no repeating groups, no partial dependency on part of a composite key, and no
attribute that is really a fact about *another* attribute rather than about the row's identity.
Lookup values move to reference tables; many-to-many relationships get junction tables.

## The normalised side — a forensic dataset

[[labour-fraud-analysis]] ships twenty tables with four reference lookups and three junction tables
(`document_person`, `document_company`, `document_worksite`) implementing the many-to-many links that
carry [[chain-of-custody]]. Foreign-key closure is asserted in two places: the database build runs
with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, so a clean build implies zero violations, and the test suite checks
primary-key uniqueness on six tables and FK closure over eight pairs. See [[reproducible-analysis]]
and [[sqlite]].

Normalisation is doing real work here, not decoration. Because a person, a company and a document are
separate entities joined through junctions, the same document can support claims about several
parties, and the [[shared-identifier-clustering]] signal is a group-by rather than a text search.

## The denormalised side — a warehouse, deliberately

[[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] goes the other way on purpose. `DIM_PRODUCT` collapses
a three-level `Product → Subcategory → Category` snowflake into one wide table, repeating category
text on every product row. That is a textbook transitive dependency and it is correct for the
workload: analytical reads, no updates, one join per dimension. See [[star-schema]].

**The rule the two repos jointly demonstrate:** normalise where the data is written and audited,
denormalise where it is only ever read in aggregate. Normal form is a property you choose per
workload, not a virtue you maximise.
